body: ADR-215's commit subject quoted a phrase. PowerShell re-quotes every argument on its way to a native .exe and the quote characters do not survive, so git re-split the argument on the spaces that had been inside them and read the pieces as PATHSPECS. Two errors, nothing committed. Then git push answered Everything up-to-date -- true, there was nothing new -- and the script printed ADR215 pushed. IT HAD BEEN WORKING BY ACCIDENT SINCE ADR-150: six manifests carry straight quotes in their bodies and every one pushed cleanly, because none of those quoted strings contains a SPACE and git splits on whitespace. So the rule is the mechanism rather than a blanket ban: --check refuses a manifest whose subject or body quotes a phrase containing a space, and ps_quote escapes a straight quote as it always did while turning a TYPOGRAPHIC one into a single quote, because that one delimits a PowerShell string as surely and cannot be escaped at all. AND THE SCRIPT SAID IT WORKED: $ErrorActionPreference Stop governs PowerShell cmdlets and says nothing about git.exe returning 1, so the failed commit ran on to the push and the push to Write-Host. ADR-203's shape and ADR-212's, except that this one is the layer those records travel on: every push script in this kit ended by printing that the slice was pushed and none of them had ever checked. Every script now reads $LASTEXITCODE after commit and stops; checks the POST-CONDITION -- this slice's own manifest in HEAD -- before pushing anything, because an exit code is what the tool says about itself and the tree is what the repository says about it; and reads $LASTEXITCODE after push. All 69 scripts are regenerated: the script is generated and never edited (ADR-184), so a generator change means every one. verify_delivery 43 to 50, mutate_delivery 38 all killed. The first answer here was WRONG and is recorded as such: curling the straight quote produced the same failure one character along, because a typographic double quote delimits a PowerShell string too and cannot be escaped at all.
subject: ADR-217: a quoted phrase with a space in it cost a commit, and the script said it had pushed
